files.README.md:
# Freelance Retainer Kit

Turn one-off projects into steady monthly income. This kit walks you from
"should I offer a retainer?" to a signed, well-run monthly arrangement.

## What's inside

| File | What it's for | Time needed |
|---|---|---|
| retainer-pricing-worksheet.md | Work out a monthly price that pays your target rate, with a worked example | 20 min |
| retainer-offer-template.md | A one-page retainer offer to send a client, plus a completed example | 30 min |
| retainer-terms-checklist.md | The 14 points every retainer agreement should settle before you start | 15 min |
| retainer-emails.md | Nine emails: pitching, renewing, overages, rollover, pausing and ending | Copy as needed |
| monthly-retainer-report.md | A short monthly report that shows the client what they got | 15 min a month |
| retainer-hours-tracker.csv | Track hours and requests against the monthly allowance | 2 min a day |

## How to use it

1. **Pick the client.** The best retainer clients already send you work most
   months, pay on time and have ongoing needs (content, maintenance, design
   support, bookkeeping, social media). Use the "Is this client a good fit?"
   check at the top of the pricing worksheet.
2. **Price it.** Fill in the worksheet. It takes your target hourly rate,
   adds the hidden time a retainer brings (check-ins, reports, context
   switching), and gives you three price points.
3. **Write the offer.** Copy the offer template, fill the brackets, and cut
   anything that doesn't apply. Keep it to one page.
4. **Send it.** Use Email 1 or Email 2 from retainer-emails.md. Most clients
   want a short call before agreeing; that's normal.
5. **Agree the terms in writing.** Go through retainer-terms-checklist.md
   and make sure your contract or written agreement covers every point.
6. **Run it.** Log every task in the hours tracker. Send the monthly report
   in the first three working days of each month, with the next invoice.
7. **Review every quarter.** If you're regularly over the allowance, use
   Email 5 to move the client up a tier.

## Opening the tracker

The .csv file opens in Excel, Google Sheets, Numbers or LibreOffice. In
Google Sheets use File > Import > Upload. Keep the header row; add one row
per task.

## A note on contracts

This kit gives you general information and templates, not legal advice.
Laws on contracts, notice periods and late payment differ by country. If a
retainer is a large part of your income, have your agreement reviewed by a
qualified professional where you work.

# Monthly Retainer Report

Send this with each invoice, in the first three working days of the month.
It takes about 15 minutes if you've kept the hours tracker up to date. A
client who can see what they got rarely questions the invoice.

---

## TEMPLATE

**[Client] | [Month Year] retainer report**
Plan: [plan], [hours] hours per month

### Summary

[One or two sentences: the most useful thing you did this month and why it
matters to the client.]

### Hours

| | Hours |
|---|---|
| Included this month | |
| Rolled over from last month | |
| Available | |
| Used | |
| Remaining / rolling over | |
| Extra hours (billed separately) | |

### Delivered

| Date | Task | Hours | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| | | | |

### Waiting on you

- [Anything you need from the client: approvals, information, access]

### Planned for next month

- [Item]
- [Item]

### Suggestions

- [One idea that would help the client. Optional, but this is where
  upgrades and new projects usually start.]

---

Plan: Standard, 16 hours per month

### Summary

already the clinic's most visited page this month. The new booking
instructions are now on every service page.

| Included this month | 16 |
| Rolled over from last month | 0 |
| Available | 16 |
| Used | 15.25 |
| Remaining / rolling over | 0.75 |
| Extra hours (billed separately) | 0 |

### Delivered

| Date | Task | Hours | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| 3 Apr | Check-in call and plan for April | 0.75 | |
| 7 Apr | Article: Back pain at your desk | 4.5 | Published 10 Apr |
| 14 Apr | April newsletter | 3 | Sent 15 Apr |
| 17 Apr | Booking instructions on 6 service pages | 1.5 | |

### Waiting on you

- May newsletter

### Suggestions

  for their members could bring in new patients. Happy to quote it.
files.retainer-emails.md:
# Retainer Emails

Nine emails for the life of a retainer. Replace everything in [brackets]
and adjust the tone to match how you normally write to the client.

---

## 1. Suggesting a retainer to an existing client

**Subject:** An easier way to book your monthly [service]

Hi [Name],

I've really enjoyed working on [recent project] with you. Looking back,
you've asked me for [type of work] in [number] of the last [number] months,
and I think there's an easier way to handle it.

Instead of quoting each piece separately, I could set aside a fixed number
of hours for you each month for a set fee. You'd get guaranteed time in my
schedule, faster turnaround, and one predictable cost.

I've put together a short one-page outline with three options. Would you
like me to send it over, or would a 15-minute call be easier?

Best,
[Your name]

---

## 2. Sending the offer

**Subject:** Monthly [service] options for [Company]

Hi [Name],

As promised, here's the outline for monthly support. In short:

- [Light]: [hours] hours, [price] per month
- [Standard]: [hours] hours, [price] per month (my recommendation, based on
  the last few months)
- [Plus]: [hours] hours, [price] per month

Full details, including how extra hours and rollover work, are in the
attached page. I could start on [date].

Happy to answer any questions.

[Your name]

---

## 3. Following up when there's no reply

**Subject:** Re: Monthly [service] options for [Company]

Hi [Name],

Just checking this reached you. No pressure either way. If the timing
isn't right, I'm happy to keep quoting work as it comes up.

If it would help, I can also start with a three-month trial on the
[Light] plan so you can see how it works.

[Your name]

---

## 4. Confirming the start

**Subject:** Confirmed: your [plan] retainer starts [date]

Hi [Name],

Great to have this set up. To confirm:

- Plan: [plan], [hours] hours per month
- Fee: [price], invoiced on the [1st] of each month, due within [number]
  days
- Start: [date]. First invoice attached.
- Requests: send them to [email address]. I'll confirm within [one working
  day].
- Monthly check-in: I'll send a calendar invite for [day/time].

Could you reply "agreed" to confirm, or sign and return the attached
agreement?

Looking forward to it.
[Your name]

---

## 5. Approaching the monthly limit

**Subject:** Hours update for [month]

Hi [Name],

A quick heads-up: we've used [hours] of this month's [hours] hours. The
requests still open are:

- [Request 1], about [hours] hours
- [Request 2], about [hours] hours

That would take us about [hours] hours over. Which would you prefer?

1. I go ahead, and the extra [hours] hours are billed at [rate] ([total]).
2. I move [request] to next month's hours.

[If this is the second or third month in a row:] We've gone over in [number]
of the last [number] months. The [next plan] plan at [price] might work out
better value. Happy to switch from next month if you'd like.

[Your name]

---

## 6. Monthly report and invoice

**Subject:** [Month] report and invoice

Hi [Name],

Here's a summary of [month]:

- Delivered: [item], [item], [item]
- Hours used: [hours] of [hours] ([hours] rolled over to next month)
- Coming up next month: [item], [item]

Full report and [month] invoice attached. Thanks as always.

[Your name]

---

## 7. Renewal or price review

**Subject:** Your retainer: looking ahead to [next period]

Hi [Name],

We've now been working together monthly for [length]. In that time we've
[result, e.g. published 18 articles and grown newsletter sign-ups].

From [date, at least 30 days away], the [plan] fee will be [new price] per
month (currently [old price]). This reflects [reason, e.g. a year of rising
costs and the extra social posts we added in spring]. Everything else stays
the same.

If you'd like to talk about the plan or adjust the hours, just reply.

[Your name]

---

## 8. Pausing the retainer

**Subject:** Pausing your retainer for [month(s)]

Hi [Name],

Thanks for letting me know about [reason]. Here's how a pause would work:

- Pause from [date] to [date]. No invoices during that time.
- [Unused hours]: the [hours] rolled-over hours [will expire / will be kept
  for when we restart].
- I can't guarantee the same availability when we restart, but I'll do my
  best to fit you in within [timeframe].

Let me know if that works and I'll confirm in writing.

[Your name]

---

## 9. Ending the retainer

**Subject:** Ending our monthly arrangement

Hi [Name],

[Thank you for letting me know / I'm writing to let you know] that the
retainer will end on [date, in line with the notice period].

Before then I'll:

- Finish [open work]
- Send you all files and logins for [items]
- Send a final invoice for [final month / any extra hours]

It's been a pleasure working with you. If you need help with a project in
the future, I'd be glad to hear from you.

[Your name]

# Retainer Offer Template

Send this as a one-page document (PDF or in the body of an email) after
you've mentioned the idea to the client. Replace everything in [brackets].
A completed example follows the template.

---

## TEMPLATE

**Monthly [service] support for [Client name]**
Prepared by [Your name], [date]

### Why a retainer

Over the last [number] months I've helped you with [types of work]. A
monthly arrangement means:

- Your work is booked in every month, so you don't wait for a free slot
- One predictable monthly cost instead of separate quotes
- Faster turnaround: [response time] on new requests
- A short monthly report so you can see exactly what was done

### What's included

[Plan name], [number] hours per month, which typically covers:

- [Deliverable 1]
- [Deliverable 2]
- [Deliverable 3]
- A [length] check-in call each month
- A written monthly report

### Options

| | [Light] | [Standard] | [Plus] |
|---|---|---|---|
| Hours per month | | | |
| Typically covers | | | |
| Response time | | | |
| Monthly fee | | | |

### How it works

- **Billing:** Invoiced on the [1st] of each month, in advance. Payment due
  within [number] days.
- **Unused hours:** [Up to X hours roll over to the next month only / Unused
  hours don't roll over.]
- **Extra work:** If a month needs more than the included hours, I'll tell
  you before going over. Extra hours are [rate] per hour, or we can move
  the work to next month.
- **Not included:** [Large projects, third-party costs, printing, etc.].
  These are quoted separately.
- **Commitment:** [Minimum term], then month to month. Either of us can end
  the arrangement with [notice period] written notice.

### Next step

Reply to let me know which option suits you, or if you'd like to talk it
through. I can start on [start date].

[Your name]
[Contact details]

---

## COMPLETED EXAMPLE

**Monthly content support for Riverside Physio**
Prepared by Sam Taylor, 3 March

### Why a retainer

Over the last six months I've helped you with blog posts, your patient
newsletter and website updates. A monthly arrangement means:

- Your content is booked in every month, so it goes out on schedule
- One predictable monthly cost instead of separate quotes
- Faster turnaround: two working days on new requests
- A short monthly report so you can see exactly what was done

### What's included

Standard plan, 16 hours per month, which typically covers:

- Two researched blog posts of 800 to 1,000 words
- The monthly patient newsletter
- Small website text updates (opening hours, team bios, service pages)
- A 30-minute check-in call each month
- A written monthly report

### Options

| | Light | Standard | Plus |
|---|---|---|---|
| Hours per month | 10 | 16 | 24 |
| Typically covers | 1 blog post + newsletter | 2 blog posts + newsletter + web updates | Standard + social posts for each article |
| Response time | 3 working days | 2 working days | Next working day |
| Monthly fee | $550 | $840 | $1,220 |

### How it works

- **Billing:** Invoiced on the 1st of each month, in advance. Payment due
  within 14 days.
- **Unused hours:** Up to 3 hours roll over to the next month only.
- **Extra work:** If a month needs more than 16 hours, I'll tell you before
  going over. Extra hours are $58 per hour, or we can move the work to next
  month.
- **Not included:** Website redesign, photography, paid advertising and
  printing. These are quoted separately.
- **Commitment:** A 3-month minimum, then month to month. Either of us can
  end the arrangement with 30 days' written notice.

### Next step

Reply to let me know which option suits you, or if you'd like to talk it
through. I can start on 1 April.

Sam Taylor
[email address]

---

## Tips

- Lead with what the client gets (reliability, speed, a fixed cost), not
  with what you get (steady income).
- Keep "what's included" in outcomes the client recognises ("two blog
  posts"), and keep hours as the limit underneath.
- If they push back on price, offer the lighter plan rather than a
  discount on the one they want.

# Retainer Pricing Worksheet

Work through the five steps in order. A completed example follows each step
so you can see the maths.

---

## Before you start: is this client a good fit?

Tick each that is true. Four or more ticks: offer a retainer. Two or fewer:
keep them on project pricing for now.

- [ ] They have sent you work in at least 3 of the last 6 months
- [ ] The work is ongoing, not a single big project
- [ ] They pay invoices on time
- [ ] They have a clear contact person who can approve work
- [ ] You'd be happy working with them for another 12 months
- [ ] Their requests are reasonably predictable in size

**Example:** A small physiotherapy clinic that has asked for blog posts and
newsletter edits 5 of the last 6 months, pays within a week, and has one
practice manager who signs off. Five ticks. Good fit.

---

## Step 1: Estimate the monthly work

Look back at the last 3 to 6 months of work for this client. Average it.

| Type of task | Typical hours per month |
|---|---|
| [Task 1] | |
| [Task 2] | |
| [Task 3] | |
| **Core hours (A)** | |

**Example:**

| Type of task | Typical hours per month |
|---|---|
| Two blog posts (research, write, edit) | 8 |
| Monthly newsletter | 3 |
| Website text updates | 2 |
| **Core hours (A)** | **13** |

---

## Step 2: Add the retainer overhead

Retainers bring time that projects don't: regular check-ins, the monthly
report, small quick questions, and switching back into the client's world.
Add it now, or you'll do it for free.

| Overhead | Hours per month |
|---|---|
| Monthly check-in call (incl. prep) | |
| Monthly report and invoice | |
| Quick questions and messages | |
| **Overhead hours (B)** | |
| **Total hours (C = A + B)** | |

A sensible rule of thumb: overhead is usually 15 to 25 percent of core
hours. If your number is much lower, check you haven't missed something.

**Example:**

| Overhead | Hours per month |
|---|---|
| 30-minute check-in call + 15 min prep | 0.75 |
| Monthly report and invoice | 0.75 |
| Quick questions and messages | 1.5 |
| **Overhead hours (B)** | **3** |
| **Total hours (C)** | **16** |

---

## Step 3: Set the base price

Base price = Total hours (C) x your target hourly rate.

| | |
|---|---|
| Target hourly rate (R) | |
| Base price (C x R) | |

**Example:** 16 hours x $55 = **$880 per month**.

---

## Step 4: Decide the discount (if any)

A small discount can be fair, because a retainer gives you predictable
income and saves you time finding work. Never discount below your minimum
acceptable rate.

| Commitment length | Typical discount |
|---|---|
| Month to month, 30 days' notice | 0% |
| 3-month minimum | 0-5% |
| 6-month minimum | 5-10% |

**Example:** The clinic agrees to a 3-month minimum. 5% off $880 = $836.
Rounded to **$840 per month**.

Check: $840 / 16 hours = $52.50 per hour. Still above the $50 minimum.
Good.

---

## Step 5: Build three options

Clients pick more easily from three choices. Make the middle one the one
you want them to choose.

| | Light | Standard | Plus |
|---|---|---|---|
| Hours included | | | |
| What that covers | | | |
| Response time | | | |
| Monthly price | | | |
| Extra hours | | | |

**Example:**

| | Light | Standard | Plus |
|---|---|---|---|
| Hours included | 10 | 16 | 24 |
| What that covers | 1 blog post + newsletter | 2 blog posts + newsletter + web updates | Standard + social posts for each article |
| Response time | 3 working days | 2 working days | Next working day |
| Monthly price | $550 | $840 | $1,220 |
| Extra hours | $60/h | $58/h | $55/h |

Notice that the per-hour price falls slightly as the plan grows, and extra
hours always cost more than included hours. That gives the client a reason
to pick the right plan instead of relying on overages.

---

## Quick reference: your numbers

| | |
|---|---|
| Client | |
| Core hours (A) | |
| Overhead hours (B) | |
| Total hours (C) | |
| Target rate (R) | |
| Minimum acceptable rate | |
| Base price | |
| Discount and reason | |
| Final monthly price | |
| Effective hourly rate | |
| Extra-hour rate | |

# Retainer Terms Checklist

Before the first invoice, make sure your written agreement settles each of
these points. Most retainer disputes come from one of them being left
vague. Tick each one off and note where it's covered.

This is general information, not legal advice. Contract rules vary by
country; get professional advice if you're unsure.

| # | Point to settle | Example wording to adapt | Covered? |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Who the agreement is between** | Full names or business names and contact details for both sides | [ ] |
| 2 | **Start date and minimum term** | "Starts 1 April. Minimum term three months, then continues month to month." | [ ] |
| 3 | **What's included** | "Up to 16 hours per month of content writing and website text updates." | [ ] |
| 4 | **What's not included** | "Website redesign, photography and paid ads are quoted separately." | [ ] |
| 5 | **The monthly fee and when it's invoiced** | "$840 per month, invoiced in advance on the 1st." | [ ] |
| 6 | **Payment terms and late payment** | "Payment due within 14 days. Work pauses if an invoice is more than 14 days overdue." | [ ] |
| 7 | **Unused hours** | "Up to 3 unused hours roll over to the following month only, then expire." | [ ] |
| 8 | **Extra hours** | "Work beyond the monthly allowance is billed at $58 per hour, approved in writing before it starts." | [ ] |
| 9 | **How requests are made** | "Requests by email to one address. Requests after 3pm count from the next working day." | [ ] |
| 10 | **Response and turnaround times** | "Acknowledged within one working day; delivered within two working days unless agreed otherwise." | [ ] |
| 11 | **Who approves work** | "The practice manager approves all work. Two rounds of changes per item are included." | [ ] |
| 12 | **Ownership of the work** | "Client owns final delivered work once that month's invoice is paid." | [ ] |
| 13 | **Price reviews** | "Fees are reviewed every 12 months, with 30 days' notice of any change." | [ ] |
| 14 | **Ending the agreement** | "After the minimum term, either side may end with 30 days' written notice. Work in progress is completed and billed." | [ ] |

## Common mistakes to avoid

- **Unlimited rollover.** Hours piling up for months turn into a debt you
  owe in time. Cap rollover, and make rolled-over hours expire.
- **"Unlimited small requests."** There's no such thing. Count everything
  in the tracker, even five-minute jobs.
- **Billing in arrears.** Retainers are normally invoiced in advance. You're
  reserving time for the client; they pay to reserve it.
- **No pause rule.** Decide now what happens if the client goes quiet for a
  month: do they still pay? (Usually yes; that's what a retainer is.)
- **Several people sending requests.** Agree one approver. Otherwise you'll
  be pulled between conflicting instructions.

## Where are these points written?

| Document | Date agreed | Where it's saved |
|---|---|---|
| Signed agreement or accepted proposal | | |
| Email confirming plan and start date | | |
| Any later changes (price, plan, hours) | | |
